newsitem.title: CANADA: Most Canadian banks signed on to Mondex cash card.
newsitem.headline: Most Canadian banks signed on to Mondex cash card.

text.p: Mondex International Ltd unit Mondex Canada said on Wednesday that four more Canadian financial companies agreed to test and participate in the rollout of the Mondex cash card.

Bank of Montreal, Canada Trust, Le Mouvement des caisses Desjardins and National Bank of Canada said they were joining Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, Royal Bank of Canada and others as participants in Mondex Canada.

Mondex Canada said Toronto-Dominion Bank was in the process of joining Mondex. Bank of Nova Scotia was the only one of Canada's six major banks that had not signed or announced a likely deal with Mondex.

Mondex Canada spokesman Joe Clark said some of the banks had a 6.4 percent equity position in Mondex International Ltd, which is 51 percent owned by MasterCard International and widely held by other financial institutions around the world.
Bank of Montreal and Canada Trust said they intended to join Canadian Imperial, Credit Union Central of Canada and Hong Kong Bank of Canada in the testing of Mondex cash cards in Guelph, Ontario.
Bank of Montreal, Canada Trust and Toronto-Dominion said they would continue to participate in testing Exact, a competing electronic cash card in Kingston, Ontario. Exact is a Belgian-based system.
Clark said that Mondex intended to begin rolling out its cash card to other communities in Canada in 1998.
